B. Is this measure already running in Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: In a Moscow cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage NSCLC, those who quit after diagnosis had an adjusted all-cause mortality HR of 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85) compared with those who kept smoking; the study compared quitters with continuing smokers, not patients offered a cessation programme.
supported_en: Annals of Internal Medicine (2021): quitting after diagnosis was linked to HR 0.67 for all-cause mortality in 517 smokers with early-stage NSCLC.
not_supported_en: No source shows how many patients offered cessation at the first visit actually quit, so the effect across everyone reached is likely smaller than 0.67.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway page says patients meet a nurse for guidance at the first visit and that quitting smoking is key to prognosis. VAKE lists a free, self-guided HUS Terveyskylä quit programme, but neither page shows a cessation programme with medication started at the first visit. A 2021 Annals of Internal Medicine cohort study found HR 0.67 (0.53–0.85) for all-cause mortality among early-stage NSCLC patients who quit, compared with those who kept smoking. That figure applies to people who actually quit, not to everyone offered the programme.
unanswered_en: No page showed whether HUS lung clinics (including Peijas) have a cessation nurse or a standing order for cessation medication for lung cancer patients.
